name: Pumpkin Spice Latte
description: A homemade PSL with real pumpkin, warm spice and maple. Better than the café version.

steps.text: Whisk the milk, pumpkin, maple syrup, spice and vanilla in a small pan over low heat until steaming.
Froth it with a frother or a quick whisk if you want some foam.
Brew your espresso or strong coffee into a mug and pour the pumpkin milk over it.
Top with whipped cream and a pinch more spice.

sources.name: Love and Lemons — Pumpkin spice latte

name: Caramel Macchiato
description: Vanilla syrup, steamed milk and espresso poured on top, finished with a caramel crosshatch.

steps.text: Put the vanilla syrup in the bottom of a tall glass or mug.
Steam the milk with a little foam and pour it over the syrup.
Pull a double espresso and pour it slowly through the foam so it sits on top.
Drizzle caramel sauce in a crosshatch over the foam.

tips: Iced version: syrup, cold milk, ice, then espresso and caramel on top.

name: Vanilla Latte
description: The café staple: a latte sweetened with vanilla syrup.

steps.text: Add the vanilla syrup to your cup.
Pull a double espresso on top and stir.
Steam the milk until silky and pour it in.

tips: DIY syrup: simmer equal parts sugar and water until dissolved, then add 1 tsp vanilla extract per 100 ml.

sources.name: Majesty Coffee — Caramel macchiato vs vanilla latte

name: Honey Cinnamon Latte
description: Espresso sweetened with honey, with cinnamon-warmed milk. Cosy and not too sweet.

steps.text: Brew espresso or strong coffee and stir the honey in while it's hot.
Warm the milk with the cinnamon (and vanilla), then froth.
Pour the milk over the coffee and dust with a little more cinnamon.

tips: For iced: shake cold milk with cinnamon in a jar and pour it over ice and the honeyed espresso.

sources.name: Emily Laurae — Honey latte with cinnamon
Half Baked Harvest — Iced cinnamon honey latte

name: Maple Cinnamon Latte
description: Maple syrup and a pinch of cinnamon turn a plain latte into an autumn treat.

steps.text: Stir the maple syrup, cinnamon and vanilla into hot espresso or strong coffee.
Steam or froth the milk.
Pour the milk over the coffee and finish with a light dusting of cinnamon.

sources.name: The Chunky Chef — Maple cinnamon latte
Tara's Multicultural Table — Maple cinnamon latte

name: Mexican Mocha
description: A mocha spiced with cinnamon and a whisper of cayenne heat.

steps.text: Mix the cocoa, sugar, cinnamon and cayenne in a mug.
Pour in the hot espresso or strong coffee and stir until there are no lumps.
Heat the milk (froth it if you can) and pour it in.
Top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon.

name: Irish Coffee
description: Hot sweetened coffee and Irish whiskey under a float of cold, lightly whipped cream.

steps.text: Warm a stemmed glass with hot water, then empty it.
Brew strong coffee (a French press is ideal).
Whip the cream just until it thickens but still pours. No stiff peaks.
Stir the brown sugar into about 120 ml of hot coffee in the glass until dissolved, then add the whiskey.
Pour the cream slowly over the back of a spoon so it floats. Don't stir; drink through the cream.
Grate a little nutmeg on top if you like.

tips: The sugar makes the coffee dense enough for the cream to float, so don't skip it.

sources.name: Food52 — The Dead Rabbit's Irish coffee
Forbes — Two famous Irish coffee recipes

name: Espresso Martini
description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and fresh espresso shaken hard for a silky foam. Ends dinner and restarts the night.

steps.text: Chill a coupe or martini glass.
Pull a fresh espresso shot.
Add vodka, coffee liqueur, syrup and the espresso to a shaker filled with ice.
Shake very hard until frothy and ice-cold.
Strain into the glass and garnish with three coffee beans.

tips: Fresh, hot espresso gives the best foam. Moka pot coffee works in a pinch.

name: Carajillo
description: Espresso and Licor 43 shaken over ice. A two-ingredient after-dinner favourite in Mexico and Spain.

steps.text: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Pull a double espresso.
Shake equal parts espresso and Licor 43 with ice until the shaker is frosty, about 20 seconds.
Strain over the fresh ice and garnish with a few coffee beans.
